slot.brief: Four options giving electron gain enthalpy orders across halogens/chalcogens/N–O pair; pick the incorrect one, testing the Cl > F exception and S > O anomaly.

stem: Taking more negative electron gain enthalpy as higher in the order, which sequence is incorrect?

verdicts.working: More negative electron gain enthalpy ranks higher. The values give Cl > F > Br > I and S > Se > Te > O; O also ranks above N. Thus only N > O is incorrect.

working:
$\text{Cl}(-349)>\text{F}(-328)$; $\text{S}(-200)>\text{O}(-141)$; $\text{O}(-141)>\text{N}(+7)$ (values in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$; $>$ denotes more negative).

Independent check: More negative electron gain enthalpy ranks higher. The values give Cl > F > Br > I and S > Se > Te > O; O also ranks above N. Thus only N > O is incorrect.
solution:
More negative electron gain enthalpy ranks higher. Since $\Delta_{eg}H(\text{O})=-141\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $\Delta_{eg}H(\text{N})=+7\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$,
$$\text{O} > \text{N}$$
Hence the sequence $\text{N} > \text{O}$ is incorrect.
